verdict.rationale: PostHog's feature-flag docs describe rolling a flagged change out to 1% of users and turning it off with no redeploy. They also mention setting release conditions, scheduling changes and watching rollouts land, so a percentage rollout changed at runtime is documented. Missing for 10: any evidence of consistent or sticky bucketing of users across evaluations, explicit documentation of ramping the percentage stepwise from 1% to 100%, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can roll a flag out progressively by percentage with consistent bucketing, ramping from 1% to 100% without redeploying

citations.quote: Wrap a change in a flag, roll it out to 1% of users, watch what happens, and turn it off the moment something looks wrong – no redeploy, no hotfix.
Create flags, set release conditions, schedule changes, and watch rollouts land.
